name: Black Holes of String Theory with Three and Four Charges
short_name: Three and Four Charge Black Holes
description: The black holes of string theory whose entropy was first counted from their microscopic states: in five dimensions with three charges, Strominger and Vafa's hole and the family of Horowitz, Maldacena, and Strominger around it, and in four dimensions with four charges, the hole of Cvetič and Youm. Each charge enters the metric through a harmonic function of its own, and the horizon of the extreme hole has an area only when every charge is present.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and take every metric to be the Einstein metric, with the Ricci tensor the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. The radius $r_0$ and the charge radii $r_i$ are lengths.
history: A black hole of five dimensions, extreme and carrying three kinds of charge, was the first whose entropy was counted state by state [strominger1996, horowitz1996four]. The entropy to be matched is Jacob Bekenstein and Stephen Hawking's, $S = k_Bc^3A/4G\hbar$ for a horizon of area $A$, a quarter of the area in Planck units [bekenstein1973, hawking1975]. A gas has its entropy because many arrangements of its molecules look alike from outside, so what does a black hole have to arrange? Andrew Strominger and Cumrun Vafa set out to derive that entropy, "including the numerical factor", "by counting black hole microstates" [strominger1996].¶Since October 1995 string theory has had things to count: that month Joseph Polchinski found that Dirichlet branes, the surfaces on which open strings end, carry exactly the charges required by string duality [polchinski1995]. One kind of brane wrapped around the rolled up dimensions makes a poor black hole, since near a brane the dimensions along it shrink and those across it swell, and the horizon is left with no area [callan1996, strominger1996]. Three kinds can hold one another off: in Curtis Callan and Juan Maldacena's picture onebranes and fivebranes steady four of the hidden dimensions between them, and momentum running along the onebranes props up the fifth [callan1996]. Each kind enters the metric through a function of its own, $H_i = 1 + r_i^2/r^2$, the potential of a point charge in four dimensions of space [tseytlin1996extreme]. Arkady Tseytlin stated the pattern as a rule, "a separate harmonic function assigned to each constituent" [tseytlin1996harmonic].¶The count went up on 9 January 1996, from Strominger in Santa Barbara and Vafa at Harvard [strominger1996]. Their hole is extreme, as light as its charges allow, and supersymmetry keeps the number of states of such a hole fixed while the strength of gravity is turned up or down [horowitz1996]. So the states can be counted where gravity is weak and the hole is a loose cluster of branes, and the number still holds where gravity is strong and the cluster is a black hole [horowitz1996]. On 9 February Callan and Maldacena, at Princeton, built the same hole from $Q_1$ onebranes, $Q_5$ fivebranes, and $N$ units of momentum, and found $S = 2\pi k_B\sqrt{NQ_1Q_5}$ from the branes and from the area alike [callan1996]. Gary Horowitz, Maldacena, and Strominger wrote of these extreme counts that "it would have been very strange indeed had the two calculations yielded different results" [horowitz1996].¶Would the match survive with mass to spare, where no symmetry protects the count? On 16 March 1996 Horowitz, Maldacena, and Strominger gave the whole family of five dimensions, six parameters, "their mass, two asymptotic scalar fields and three charges" [horowitz1996]. Its metric is "just the five-dimensional Schwarzschild metric with the time and space components rescaled by different powers of $f$", their $f$ being the product $H_1H_2H_3$ [horowitz1996]. Mirjam Cvetič and Donam Youm had posted the same solutions the day before [cvetic1996rotating, horowitz1996]. Its entropy is a product of three factors, one each for the onebranes, the fivebranes, and the strings: $S = 2\pi k_B(\sqrt{N_1} + \sqrt{N_{\bar 1}})(\sqrt{N_5} + \sqrt{N_{\bar 5}})(\sqrt{n_L} + \sqrt{n_R})$, with each $N$ a number of branes or antibranes and each $n$ a number of strings moving left or right [horowitz1996]. They called the formula "surprisingly simple, but mysterious", and could derive it from the branes only in limits where the branes interact weakly [horowitz1996].¶The hole of four dimensions came first: in July 1995, at the University of Pennsylvania, Cvetič and Youm had found an extreme hole of the heterotic string on a torus of six dimensions, with two electric and two magnetic charges and a function $1 + r_i/r$ for each [cvetic1996dyonic]. Its general member has "a space-time of extreme Reissner-Nordström black holes while configurations with more constrained charges have a null or a naked singularity" [cvetic1996dyonic]. Branes alone supply three of the four charges, and the fourth needs another kind of object [maldacena1996]. Maldacena and Strominger's count appeared on 11 March 1996, with a fivebrane for the fourth charge [maldacena1996]. Clifford Johnson, Ramzi Khuri, and Robert Myers's appeared the same day, with a Kaluza-Klein monopole [johnson1996]. David Lowe joined Horowitz and Maldacena on 29 March to take the hole of four charges off extremality, where its entropy is again a product of sums of square roots [horowitz1996four].¶With the charges equal the scalar fields are constant, and the holes are familiar ones: Reissner and Nordström's in four dimensions and its counterpart in five [horowitz1996, horowitz1996four]. With two charges equal and two absent the hole of four dimensions is the dilaton black hole, and with one charge it is the Kaluza-Klein black hole [cvetic1996static]. Next to its extreme horizon the hole of five dimensions is a throat, anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a 3-sphere, the Bertotti-Robinson universe with one dimension more [strominger1996]. By 1998 the count needed neither strings nor supersymmetry: Strominger showed that wherever the geometry near a horizon is locally anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions, the growth in the number of states of a conformal field theory reproduces the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy [strominger1998].

related.text: The hole of five dimensions with no charge, $r_1 = r_2 = r_3 = 0$. Horowitz, Maldacena, and Strominger built the charged family by rescaling its time and its space by powers of $H_1H_2H_3$ [horowitz1996].
The hole of four dimensions with its four charges equal. The scalar fields are then constant, and in the areal radius $r + r_1$ the metric is Reissner and Nordström's [horowitz1996four].
The hole of four dimensions with two of its charges equal and the other two absent [cvetic1996static].
The hole of four dimensions with one charge alone, in its Einstein metric [cvetic1996static].

One harmonic function where this spacetime has four. With its four charges equal the extreme hole of four dimensions is a single hole of Majumdar and Papapetrou, an extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole [cvetic1996dyonic].

The throat of the extreme hole of four dimensions, the limit $r \to 0$ with $t$ rescaled. Its 2-spheres stop shrinking at the radius $(r_1r_2r_3r_4)^{1/4}$, and Strominger and Vafa found the same throat with a 3-sphere in five dimensions [strominger1996].

Two things done to Tangherlini's hole of five dimensions: Myers and Perry set it spinning, and string theory gives it three charges. Cvetič and Youm's rotating solution has the charges and both spins at once [cvetic1996rotating].

Charge radius of the first charge, $r_1 = r_0\sinh\alpha_1$ for a boost $\alpha_1$, a length
Charge radius of the second charge, $r_2 = r_0\sinh\alpha_2$ for a boost $\alpha_2$, a length
Charge radius of the third charge, $r_3 = r_0\sinh\alpha_3$ for a boost $\alpha_3$, a length

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$ in $D = 5$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, so $\dot{t}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(ct)/d\lambda$. The mass is $M = \pi c^2\left(3r_0^2 + 2r_1^2 + 2r_2^2 + 2r_3^2\right)/(8G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions.

parameters.description: Radius of the event horizon in the coordinate $r$ of the chart of three charges, a length; the hole is extreme at $r_0 = 0$
Common charge radius of the three equal charges, a length, and the radius of the inner horizon

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \psi, \theta, \phi)$ in $D = 5$ for three equal charges, $r_1 = r_2 = r_3 = r_q$, with $\rho^2 = r^2 + r_q^2$ the areal radius and $t$ carrying dimensions of time. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, so $\dot{t}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{\rho} + \dfrac{\left(\rho + r_q\right)\left(\rho - r_q\right)\left(\rho^2 - r_0^2 - r_q^2\right)\left(\rho^2\,r_0^2 + 2\rho^2\,r_q^2 - 2r_0^2\,r_q^2 - 2r_q^4\right)}{\rho^9}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{\rho^2\,r_0^2 + 2\rho^2\,r_q^2 - 2r_0^2\,r_q^2 - 2r_q^4}{\rho\left(\rho + r_q\right)\left(\rho - r_q\right)\left(\rho^2 - r_0^2 - r_q^2\right)}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\left(\rho + r_q\right)\left(\rho - r_q\right)\left(\rho^2 - r_0^2 - r_q^2\right)}{\rho^3}\dot{\psi}^2 - \dfrac{\left(\rho + r_q\right)\left(\rho - r_q\right)\left(\rho^2 - r_0^2 - r_q^2\right)\sin^2\psi}{\rho^3}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(\rho + r_q\right)\left(\rho - r_q\right)\left(\rho^2 - r_0^2 - r_q^2\right)\sin^2\psi\sin^2\theta}{\rho^3}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
